title: Parent discloses excessive personal data during registration

If all fields are not strictly necessary at sign-up, the act of sharing itself creates a disclosure risk because more personal data than needed is exposed to the system.

uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ depending on whether the threat tree distinguishes direct identifiers in content vs metadata.

title: Video content or metadata may identify the parent or child in transit
description: The uploaded video and its embedded metadata may directly or indirectly identify individuals, for example through faces, voices, home environment, school uniforms, geotags, filenames, or account/session identifiers carried with the upload.
assumptions: Assumes the video or accompanying metadata contains personal identifiers or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Specific tree node is approximate because the retrieved context did not provide detailed I threat-tree nodes.

title: Approval workflow reveals personal information to reviewers or internal roles
description: On receipt, the video management service may expose the uploaded video and associated account details to moderators, reviewers, or support staff, disclosing personal information beyond what the parent may expect for simple upload handling.
assumptions: Assumes human or automated review occurs and associated metadata is accessible within the service.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; detailed D nodes were not present in retrieved context.

title: Secondary use of uploaded videos beyond approval decision
description: The service may use uploaded videos or their metadata for purposes beyond approval/rejection, such as model training, analytics, content moderation tuning, fraud detection, or product improvement, without the parent's clear expectation or consent.
assumptions: Assumes the service has technical or organizational ability to repurpose uploads after receipt.
uncertainty_note: Specific U tree node is approximate because the retrieved context did not provide detailed U threat-tree nodes.

title: Improper management of uploaded child-related personal data
description: If the video management service stores, reviews, or retains uploaded videos and related metadata without appropriate legal basis, transparency, minimization, retention limits, or child-specific safeguards, the receipt and handling of this flow can create non-compliance risks.
assumptions: Assumes the uploaded video may contain personal data, potentially including children's data, and is subject to privacy regulation.

title: Streaming reveals the child's viewing activity to the service
description: By sending the approved video stream to the child, the Video Management Service necessarily learns and can expose that this specific child account/device is watching a particular approved video at a particular time. This creates detectability of the child's content-consumption activity at the source element.
assumptions: Assumes the stream request/response is associated with a child-specific account, profile, session, or device identifier rather than being fully anonymous and unlinkable.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed D threat-tree nodes.

title: Streaming metadata can link repeated viewing sessions
description: Metadata on the video stream flow, such as persistent session identifiers, IP address, device identifiers, or stable transport tokens, can allow repeated viewing sessions to be linked to the same child or household over time.
assumptions: Assumes the streaming protocol or surrounding delivery infrastructure uses stable identifiers or observable network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact L threat-tree node is selected by best judgement; retrieved context only confirmed that Linkability is applicable to Process→ExternalEntity flows.

title: Streaming metadata may identify the child or household
description: Even if the video payload itself is approved content, data in transit such as account tokens, IP address, device identifiers, or CDN/request headers may identify the child user or their household to network observers or intermediaries.
assumptions: Assumes the stream is not fully anonymized and that intermediaries or observers can access identifying metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact I threat-tree node is selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed identifiability nodes.

title: The child may be unaware of tracking or personalization tied to streaming
description: At the destination, the child user may not understand that receiving and watching the stream can trigger logging, analytics, recommendations, or parental reporting about their viewing behavior. This creates a risk of insufficient awareness regarding privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Assumes the service performs some downstream logging, analytics, recommendation, or reporting associated with playback.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on additional processing associated with playback; if the stream is delivered without any behavioral logging or secondary use, this may not apply.

title: Streaming may involve improper management of children's personal data
description: Delivering video to a child can involve processing children's personal data, such as viewing history, account identifiers, age/profile status, and device data. If the service streams and logs this data without an appropriate legal basis, age-appropriate transparency, minimization, retention limits, or parental-consent handling where required, the flow contributes to non-compliance.
assumptions: Assumes the service processes personal data related to a child and is subject to child-privacy or general data-protection obligations.
uncertainty_note: Applicability of specific legal obligations depends on jurisdiction and whether personal data beyond strictly necessary delivery is processed.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data from profiles store to recommendation engine
description: The childprofiles collection may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary to generate recommendations. Sending raw or broad browsing histories from the datastore to the AI engine can violate data minimization, especially given the sensitivity of children's behavioral data.
assumptions: Assumes the AI engine could operate on a reduced feature set, aggregated signals, or pseudonymized inputs rather than full browsing records.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization structure; exact subnode may differ in your local taxonomy.

title: Recommendation engine may use child browsing data for an unexpected purpose
description: Once received, the AI Recommendation Engine may process child browsing data for purposes beyond the user's or guardian's reasonable expectations, such as model training, profiling refinement, experimentation, or secondary analytics rather than only producing immediate recommendations.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation and expectation management are not clearly defined for this planned flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subnode is inferred from typical LINDDUN unawareness/purpose-expansion threats; verify against your threat tree.

title: Insufficient transparency or valid consent for using child browsing data in AI recommendations
description: Using children's browsing data in an AI recommendation engine may require clear notice, parental authorization, and/or another valid legal basis. If the planned processing is not transparently communicated or consent/authorization is not properly obtained and managed, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to child-privacy and data-protection obligations and that this AI use may be new or materially different from the original collection context.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and product context; exact Nc subnode may vary.

title: AI engine can link browsing data with other child identifiers or profiles
description: After receipt, the AI engine may combine browsing data from the childprofiles collection with account identifiers, device identifiers, household data, or historical interactions, enabling stronger linkage of records to the same child across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes P4 has access to additional identifiers or correlated datasets.
uncertainty_note: Specific L subnode is best-effort; linkage risk is clear but exact taxonomy leaf should be checked.

title: Child may become identifiable through rich browsing behavior processed by the AI engine
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent from the transferred dataset, detailed browsing patterns can act as quasi-identifiers. The AI engine may infer or single out a specific child when combined with other available data, making the child identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes browsing histories are sufficiently granular and P4 can access auxiliary data or high-dimensional behavioral features.
uncertainty_note: Identification from behavioral data is context-dependent; exact I leaf may differ.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine plans to send users' browsing data to third-party advertisers. This is a direct disclosure of personal data across a system boundary and may violate data minimization if the advertisers do not strictly need the full browsing data for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Browsing data relates to identifiable or reasonably linkable users and is not strictly necessary to share in raw or detailed form with advertisers.

title: Further disclosure or secondary use of browsing data by advertisers
description: Once received, third-party advertisers may store, combine, profile, or onward-share the browsing data for additional advertising, analytics, or brokerage purposes beyond the original context in which the data was collected.
assumptions: Advertisers are separate controllers/processors with their own data ecosystems and may reuse received data unless contractually and technically constrained.
uncertainty_note: Exact downstream uses are not specified in the flow description, but such secondary use is a common and credible risk for advertiser recipients.

title: Cross-context linking of user activity by third-party advertisers
description: Advertisers can combine the received browsing data with identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or existing profiles from other sources to link a user's activity across services and contexts.
assumptions: The browsing data contains direct identifiers, persistent pseudonyms, or sufficiently distinctive behavioral attributes that enable correlation with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed L threat-tree nodes.

title: Identification of users from shared browsing data
description: Detailed browsing histories or associated identifiers may allow advertisers to identify specific individuals directly or indirectly, especially when combined with existing customer or ad-tech datasets.
assumptions: Shared browsing data includes identifiers or quasi-identifiers, or is granular enough to single out individuals when combined with auxiliary information.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement threat-tree node; applicability depends on the granularity and identifiability of the browsing data actually shared.

title: Inference of sensitive interests from browsing data
description: Advertisers may infer sensitive attributes such as health concerns, political views, religion, sexual orientation, or financial distress from users' browsing behavior, even if such attributes are not explicitly transmitted.
assumptions: Browsing data includes URLs, page categories, search/referral context, timestamps, or other signals from which sensitive traits can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement threat-tree node; the exact sensitivity depends on the categories of browsing data included in DF14.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Sending browsing data from the recommendation engine to third-party advertisers may be incompatible with the original collection context unless users were clearly informed and gave valid consent or another appropriate legal basis exists.
assumptions: Users provided browsing data primarily for recommendations or service delivery, not necessarily for third-party advertising disclosures.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement threat-tree node; legal basis and notice details are not provided in the flow description.

title: Collection and storage of excessive identity-document data
description: The authentication service stores full government ID images in the file system. Full document images typically contain more personal data than is strictly necessary for many authentication purposes (e.g., document number, nationality, MRZ, photo, address), creating an avoidable disclosure through over-collection and persistence.
assumptions: Assumes the service could achieve its purpose with less data than full image retention, such as extracted attributes, redacted images, or short-lived verification artifacts.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best-fit judgement for explicit/avoidable disclosure via non-minimal collection/storage; exact subnode may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Unnecessary retention of government ID images in backend storage
description: Once received by the file system, government ID images may be retained longer than necessary for authentication, increasing exposure of highly sensitive identity data. Storing raw images at the destination creates a privacy threat if retention is not strictly limited to the verification purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS4 persists uploaded files beyond immediate processing and that strict retention/deletion controls are not guaranteed by design.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is an informed approximation for avoidable disclosure caused by storage/retention at the destination.

title: Government ID images enable direct identification of the data subject
description: The destination stores raw government ID images, which inherently contain strong identifiers such as name, photograph, document number, and date of birth. Receipt and storage of these images makes the individual directly identifiable from the data held in DS4.
assumptions: Assumes uploaded images are readable and stored in a form accessible to system components or administrators.
uncertainty_note: Identification is strongly supported by the nature of government ID images; subnode id is best-fit.

title: Stored ID images can be linked across sessions or services
description: Persisting government ID images in backend storage enables correlation of the same person across multiple authentication attempts, accounts, or related services, especially if filenames, metadata, or extracted document identifiers are reused. This creates a linkability threat beyond the immediate authentication event.
assumptions: Assumes DS4 or connected components can associate stored images or derived identifiers with repeated interactions or other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on surrounding system design and metadata practices; applicability is plausible but somewhat context-dependent, and the subnode id is approximate.

title: Storage of ID images may exceed user expectations or stated purpose
description: Users may provide government ID images for one-time identity verification, but storing them in backend/uploads/ can conflict with expectations if the storage purpose, duration, or downstream use is not transparent and aligned with consent or notice. This creates a non-compliance risk around purpose limitation, transparency, and data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the system's notice/consent and retention policy do not clearly justify persistent storage of raw ID images.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on the actual legal basis, notices, and retention policy; tree-node id is best-fit rather than citation-backed from the provided context.

title: JWT in localStorage can identify the user or device
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage makes a persistent token available to scripts running in the browser context. If the token contains user identifiers or stable claims, the destination data store enables identification of the user or browser profile when the token is later read and used.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifying claims such as subject, account id, email, tenant id, or similarly unique attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort based on general LINDDUN identification semantics; exact sub-node may differ in your catalog.

title: Persistent JWT storage enables cross-session linkability
description: A JWT stored in localStorage persists across page loads and browser sessions until explicitly removed. This stable token can link multiple actions, visits, or transactions performed from the same browser profile over time.
assumptions: Assumes the same token or stable token-derived identifier is reused across multiple requests or sessions.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node granularity may vary; threat applicability is strong because persistence in localStorage directly supports linking.

title: JWT contents may disclose personal data to browser-side code
description: If the JWT payload contains personal data, roles, tenant information, or other sensitive claims, storing it in localStorage exposes that information to any script executing in the origin, increasing the chance of privacy-relevant disclosure beyond the minimum necessary use.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not an opaque reference token and contains readable claims, as is common for JWTs.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure depends on token contents; if the JWT is opaque or encrypted and inaccessible to scripts, impact is reduced.

title: localStorage persistence may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Users may not expect authentication tokens to be stored persistently in browser localStorage, especially across sessions or logout edge cases. This can conflict with data minimization, storage limitation, or consent/choice expectations if retention and purpose are not clearly communicated and controlled.
assumptions: Assumes token persistence duration, logout clearing behavior, or notice/consent mechanisms are not explicitly aligned with user expectations and policy.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on the applicable legal basis, notices, retention policy, and implementation details not provided here.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: The Child Profile Management process may disclose more of the child's history than is necessary for the parent's immediate review purpose, revealing sensitive behavioral, educational, or health-related details beyond what is proportionate.
assumptions: Assumes the child history can contain sensitive or longitudinal records and that not all retrieved fields are strictly necessary for each parent review interaction.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure at the source; exact sub-node may differ in the project taxonomy.

title: Identification of child or parent via data in transit
description: The transmitted child history and associated metadata may directly identify the child and parent, or make them identifiable through names, account identifiers, timestamps, or contextual details present on the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries account-linked history rather than fully anonymized content.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may vary depending on whether identification is direct or indirect.

title: Linking of child records across interactions
description: Recurring identifiers or stable metadata on this flow can allow different history items and review sessions to be linked together, enabling construction of a richer profile of the child and the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Assumes repeated retrievals use stable identifiers, session data, or consistent contextual attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node chosen from general LINDDUN linking taxonomy; exact sub-node not provided in retrieved context.

title: Further disclosure by parent recipient
description: Once received, the parent user may store, share, screenshot, or otherwise redistribute the child's history outside the intended context, causing additional disclosure of the child's personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the system cannot fully control onward sharing by the external recipient.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side disclosure risk grounded in recipient handling; exact sub-node may differ.

title: Unawareness of child about parental access to history
description: The child may be unaware that their history is being retrieved and reviewed by the parent, including what categories of information are visible and under what conditions access occurs.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly inform the child about parental visibility into their history.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may vary depending on whether the taxonomy distinguishes lack of notice from lack of transparency.

title: Non-compliant parental access to child history
description: Providing child history to the parent may violate applicable privacy, child-protection, or consent rules if access is not properly limited by the child's age, legal basis, custody status, or jurisdiction-specific requirements.
assumptions: Assumes legal or policy constraints may apply to parental access to certain child records.
uncertainty_note: Compliance applicability is context-dependent; exact legal basis is not provided, so this threat is conditional.
